title: Six concyclic points satisfy the Euclidean Ramsey tensor criterion, as does every spherical set of at most m + 4 points of affine dimension m and every algebraic spherical set; given the classification's sufficiency half, these sets are Ramsey (the algebraic ones when spanning)
summary: A Lean 4 development around the tensor criterion of the classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations (openai/math, family 172). With the criterion's definitions restated character for character from that project's challenge file: every set of six distinct points on a circle satisfies the criterion, by an explicit certificate (the product of the two bilinear forms through the first three and the last three points of a homogeneous parametrisation of the circle, scaled and conjugated by the parametrisation); the sharp dimension theorem: every spherical set of at most m + 4 distinct…

review.reason: Lean development on Euclidean Ramsey criteria for spherical point configurations.
